subject: Post-demo: finalizing p95/p99 acceptance criteria and streaming concurrency handshake
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@orbitalai.com>, Kyle Turner <kyle.turner@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: p95/p99 targets and next steps

Hi Samantha, Kyle —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of the perf items we agreed to validate and the immediate asks so we can finalize the SLOs for the pilot:

1) Targets we discussed
   - Orbital target: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 720ms (end-to-end, production-like traffic)
   - Current incumbent: you said p95 ~ 400ms, p99 ~ 1.4s on your live traffic profile

2) Workstreams and owners
   - Redwood runbook & test harness: Ben & Marissa (will run hosted API and controlled incumbent runs)
   - Traffic profile export / sample keys: Samantha (you to provide a small redacted trace and a test API key)
   - Acceptance criteria: Jonas (sales) will collate results into the MAU and SLO doc for procurement.

3) Constraints and clarifying questions (please confirm):
   - Sustained concurrency window: 100 concurrent streaming sessions for 15s bursts (typical billing window)
   - Max sustained throughput baseline to test: 1,200 requests/min (mix of short and long sequences, avg tokens/req ~ 45)
   - Streaming behavior: client uses chunked streaming; tail completion messages are critical (we need identical reassembly semantics)

Next steps I propose:
   - Samantha: send the small traffic sample + a test token (can be scoped) — target by Tue 6/17 EOD
   - Ben & Marissa: prepare runbook and a hosted vs incumbent test matrix (deliverable Wed 6/18 morning)
   - Jonas: ship the acceptance checklist to your procurement and legal once we have numbers (Fri 6/20 suggested)

Attachments: I attached a starter perf profile (orbital-performance-profile.json) with the traffic mix we recorded during the demo. If you prefer, we can run the first comparison using only streaming endpoints.

Hit reply with any corrections; otherwise we’ll kick off the benchmarking run on Wednesday.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: p95/p99 targets and next steps

Jonas — thanks, this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirming targets: p95 <= 220ms and p99 <= 720ms are what our product team needs as a gating metric for rollout. p50 is not a gating metric but helpful for capacity planning.

- Streaming semantics: our client expects chunked events with a resume token for reconnection (we’ll provide the protocol doc). Important: we need stable ordering and idempotent token semantics across fallbacks.

- Traffic sample & creds: attached a scoped test token (test-harness-creds.txt) and a 10-minute trace sampled from our staging traffic. The trace has a 70/30 split streaming/plain generation.

- Throughput nuance: the 1,200 req/min was an example; our peak for this flow is closer to 1,800 req/min sustained for 5 minutes during batch runs (burst windows). If you can include a 1,800 req/min run in the matrix that would be ideal.

We’re happy to start with the 100-concurrency/15s burst and then run the higher-throughput scenario. Also please confirm whether your hosted API will preserve our streaming chunk boundaries exactly (we need to validate on the first run).

Thanks — I’ll put Kyle on the thread for infra details.

—
Samantha Li
Head of Product, Orbital AI
Orbital AI | sam@orbitalai.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: p95/p99 targets and next steps

Samantha / Jonas — pulling together the runbook now. Quick technical notes and commitments from Redwood engineering before we start:

- We will run three comparative phases:
   A) Baseline incumbent replay (your staging endpoint + our runner)
   B) Redwood hosted API (single-region US-west)
   C) Redwood hosted + read-through prefix cache (to show best-case unit-cost and latency improvements)

- Measurement specifics
   - End-to-end measurement: client send -> first response byte -> final completion (we’ll compute p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and final-completion)
   - Sampling window: 5-minute sliding windows, multiple runs per scenario (min 3 runs each)
   - Error handling: we will surface any 5xxs or stream resets; those will be excluded from latency histograms but logged in the failure report

- Concurrency/throughput coverage
   - We will run the 100 concurrent streaming sessions (15s bursts) test first.
   - We will then run sustained 1,800 req/min for 5 minutes per the sample (as requested).

- Streaming semantics validation
   - We will validate chunk boundaries and a resume-token reconnection. If we detect any reordering or missing chunks in our run, we’ll capture wire-level traces and attach as artifacts.

- Deliverables & timeline
   - Runbook + test matrix: Wed 6/18 09:00 PT
   - First comparative runs (phases A/B): Thu 6/19 — results summary by Thu 6/19 20:00 PT
   - Full throughput stress (1,800 req/min) and caching runs: Fri 6/20 — final summary by Mon 6/23

I’ll attach the run commands and the tooling config once the runbook is committed. Marissa — I’ve left a few TODOs in the runbook for you on labeling and dashboarding.

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Jonas / Ben / Samantha —

I've updated the runbook with the labeling conventions and dashboard hooks for p95/p99 and first-byte vs final-completion. A couple of operational clarifications:

- Canary window: we will do a short canary (5 min) at 50% of your peak (900 req/min) before the full 1,800 req/min stress to ensure there are no silent degradations.

- Fallback policy: if we observe p99 > 1s for two consecutive runs, the automatic fallback will switch to a lower-latency model variant and we’ll re-run the measurement (this will be clearly called out in the acceptance doc).

- Artifacts: we’ll produce a compressed artifact set with histograms, raw traces (redacted), and a short decision memo. Expect the first comparative artifact bundle Thu 6/19 20:00 PT.

Samantha — once we complete the Thu runs we’ll schedule a 30-min sync to walk through the histograms and the suggested SLO language for procurement. Does Thu 6/19 21:00 PT work for you?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Performance Engineering | Redwood Inference
